pr_title: Correctly resolve third party bevy crates via `bevy_macro_utils`
pr_body:
Fixes #17816.

## Objective

Currently `BevyManifest` incorrectly assumes all crates starting with `bevy_` are official bevy crates that are re-exported through the main `bevy` crate.

## Solution

- `BevyManifest` should handle third party crates starting with `bevy_` correctly.

## Testing

- I ran the ci.
- It should be verified that the `build.rs` does not break when uploaded to `crates.io`.

## Migration Guide

- Users of `BevyManifest::get_subcrate` should migrate to `BevyManifest::maybe_get_path` or `BevyManifest::get_path`.
pr_comments:
> I'm pretty sure convention is to use `OUT_DIR`, as `src/` is supposed to be immutable

That won't work. The file must be committed to source control.

See https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/17816#issuecomment-2660932114.
Otherwise when `bevy_macro_utils` is pulled as a dependency, it does not have the files necessary to generate the official crates list.

It is a little dirty but the best I could do. I am open to suggestions.

I marked it as a draft again because I was concerned, that publishing could trigger the following error introduced via https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/5073:
```
error: failed to verify package tarball

Caused by:
  Source directory was modified by build.rs during cargo publish. Build scripts should not modify anything outside of OUT_DIR.
...
```

I ran `cargo publish --dry-run --allow-dirty -p bevy_macro_utils` but it worked fine.

When `cargo publish` builds the package, it is being built in a separate directory: `Current working directory: "/argon_bfs/user_main/argon_bfs_desktop/bevy_dev/bevy/target/package/bevy_macro_utils-0.16.0-dev"`.
Since the parent directory is not `crates` no files in `src` are modified.
I am now confident that the `build.rs` should not cause any issues during publishing or when `bevy_macro_utils` is pulled in as dependency.

> If you know a better way just ping me and I can try to make it happen.

Could we explore the dependency tree of the `bevy` crate? I've played a bit with cargo manifest tools and think that should work; I'm just not sure if that information will be available where we need it.
I can investigate it in the coming weeks. Feel free to merge this whenever though. I will just create a new pr when I get around to doing it.

issue_context.title: `BevyManifest` incorrectly assumes that all crates starting with `bevy_` are exposed through `::bevy::`
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/153ce468efb1d596c744378be6bdb1a83dea05b8/crates/bevy_macro_utils/src/bevy_manifest.rs#L14-L18

When I modified `BevyManifest`, I thought that it was bevy internal. However it is also used by https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy_editor_prototypes/blob/f41e2240174e29f1c9206bb6b080431463466ea5/crates/bevy_bsn/src/macros/src/derive_construct.rs#L14-L16 and possibly in other crates too. As long as only official bevy crates are resolved though it, there are no issues.

However, should a user crate that extends bevy and is named `bevy_...` use the `BevyManifest` in their proc macros, it will incorrectly assume their crate is available through `::bevy::`.

A fix would be to only strip the prefix from the `bevy_` crates that are actually available through `::bevy::`.

I can create a pr for this and see two options:
1) List dir in `crates/` to get all the bevy internal crates. More complex but should automatically keep up with bevy but possibly yield wrong results if crates are added that are not rexported through bevy.
2) Just using a manual string list. Simpler but needs to be kept in sync manually.
comments: I would prefer solution 1. We would definitely desync this pretty quickly.

I investigated solution 1.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a5e0850-7e68-4eda-b3e1-47fee74d3075)

Unfortunately `bevy_macro_utils` has no way of knowing which bevy crates are official and re-exported through the `bevy` crate. I have attached an image of all the files `bevy_macro_utils` has access to, if it is downloaded as a dependency.

I can write a script to generate rust source code with a static str slice of all official bevy crates. However, I don't know how to best hook it into the build process.

review_comments: @mockersf can we share this list between this and our publishing tooling somehow?
